html:
Nizamuddin Auliya was a Sufi teacher of the Chishti order who lived in Delhi from the 1250s until his death in 1325. He is the best loved Muslim saint of north India.

He was born in Badaun and grew up poor after his father died. At twenty he became a disciple of Baba Farid in Punjab, who named him his successor. He settled at Ghiyaspur, then a village outside Delhi, and ran a hospice there for sixty years.

His teaching was that the way to God is love, and that love of God means service to people. His kitchen fed anyone who came, Hindu or Muslim. He owned nothing and gave away each day's gifts by nightfall. He kept clear of rulers: seven sultans reigned in his lifetime and he went to none of their courts. When one sultan, marching home, sent word that he should leave the city, he is said to have answered "Delhi is still far". The sultan died before he arrived.

The poet Amir Khusrau was his devoted follower and is buried beside him. The singing of qawwali at Sufi shrines goes back to their circle. His tomb in Delhi still draws crowds of every faith. See also the Chishti order.
sum: Nizamuddin Auliya was a Sufi teacher of the Chishti order who lived in Delhi from the 1250s until his death in 1325. He is the best loved Muslim saint of north India.
